examples.solution_text:
The two circular ends have total area $2\pi r^{2}$.
The curved side unrolls into a rectangle with length $2\pi r$ and width $h$, so its area is $2\pi rh$.
Adding the three faces gives $A=2\pi r^{2}+2\pi rh$.

Halve the diameter to find the radius.
$\begin{aligned}r&=\frac{14}{2}=7\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}A&=2\pi r^{2}+2\pi rh\\&=2\pi(7)^{2}+2\pi(7)(9)\\&=98\pi+126\pi\\&=224\pi\text{ cm}^{2}\\&\approx703.7\text{ cm}^{2}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: Closed cylinder A has radius $6$ cm and height $4$ cm. Closed cylinder B has radius $4$ cm and height $6$ cm. Which has the larger total surface area? Justify your answer using exact areas.
examples.solution_text:
Cylinder A:
$\begin{aligned}A&=2\pi r^{2}+2\pi rh\\&=2\pi(6)^{2}+2\pi(6)(4)\\&=72\pi+48\pi\\&=120\pi\text{ cm}^{2}\end{aligned}$
Cylinder B:
$\begin{aligned}A&=2\pi r^{2}+2\pi rh\\&=2\pi(4)^{2}+2\pi(4)(6)\\&=32\pi+48\pi\\&=80\pi\text{ cm}^{2}\end{aligned}$
Cylinder A has the larger surface area because $120\pi>80\pi$.

examples.question_text: A cylinder has radius $7$ cm and curved surface area $168\pi$ cm². Find its height.
examples.solution_text:
Use the curved surface area $2\pi rh$.
$\begin{aligned}2\pi rh&=168\pi\\2\pi(7)h&=168\pi\\14\pi h&=168\pi\\h&=12\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: A closed cylinder has radius $5$ m and total surface area $400$ m². Find its height to $1$ decimal place.

examples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}2\pi x^{2}+2\pi x(4x)&=160\pi\\2\pi x^{2}+8\pi x^{2}&=160\pi\\10\pi x^{2}&=160\pi\\x^{2}&=16\\x&=4\end{aligned}$
Take the positive square root because the radius is a positive length.

coverage.summary: Authored seven examples covering every distinct assessed method, using supplied booklet teaching and exercises with changed numerical values. Practice and quiz mathematics were neither altered nor re-audited. Questions and solutions remain separate and editable; solution prose and mathematics inherit renderer blue. Equations align at relation signs, with no bare-expression continuation requiring a phantom gutter. Native diagrams are unshaded with black marks, explicit 10 pt labels, solid visible silhouettes and dashed obscured rear rims; labels use non-drawing paths. Final-size visual verification and independent source/mathematical review remain for the coordinator.

examples.derivation: Two circular ends contribute 2πr². The unrolled side contributes (2πr)h, giving A = 2πr² + 2πrh.
A = 2π(3²) + 2π(3)(8) = 66π cm² = 207.345115… cm², rounding to 207.35 cm².
Cylinder A has area (72 + 48)π = 120π cm². Cylinder B has area (32 + 48)π = 80π cm². Cylinder A has the larger area.
2πx² + 2πx(4x) = 10πx² = 160π. Thus x² = 16 and x = 4 because the radius is positive.
